The exact reported useMutation is a controller owner. Its isPending state reaches private Add, editor Save, category and delete controls; the same parent renders a stable visible polite/atomic Saving/Saved region. Existing destructive Alert reports failure; onSuccess updates the cache and clears only intended successful drafts/intents. Deferred real-component tests verify POST pending feedback, disabled repeat activation, success/failure drafts, and one DELETE with the captured version. The scanner does not follow the controller object through extracted controls. Reconsider if a control stops consuming pending, feedback leaves this owner or mutation/intent ownership changes. Eight actual Chromium cases additionally verify keyboard pending focus, repeat activation, failures, light/dark, narrow/wide layout, reduced motion and axe through synthetic transport.

Actual window Cmd/Ctrl+K listener guards handled events, composition, repeats, modifiers, editable targets and other popups. Window bubbling preserves Support/Care shortcut ownership; non-editing own popup toggles closed.
Mission Control mounts app-owned search backed by existing role-filtered navigation and real router.push commands. Scanner cannot follow the feature component and its dynamic mapped CommandItems.
Both actual memory category controls use SelectControlLabel, the Base UI Select.Label wrapper, which associates with their trigger.
Offline gift DialogContent renders child form containing DialogTitle. Actual composed dialog is named Enter offline gift while open.

The memory query renders EveSectionEmpty only after successful resolution with no entries. EveSectionEmpty delegates to the shared Empty status region. The actual memory concurrency suite verifies empty and filtered results, avoiding a false empty state during pending queries. The scanner does not follow the derived entries and extracted status owner.
Resend renders FieldError through getRenderableErrors; credential field now exposes aria-invalid and references its error ID. Shared AppFields also own visible field errors.

The exact Undo and adjacent Redo buttons receive aria-label through Base UI TooltipTrigger render composition. The actual PDF header test queries both rendered buttons by their names. The scanner stops at the nested Button instead of following the trigger props.

The exact Item render Link receives its visible ItemTitle through Base UI composition. The rendered admin availability test resolves named Staff directory, Eve and Email delivery links. This is limited to this composed Item/Link boundary, not unnamed links generally.
Exact flagged Eve operations navigation is an always-visible responsive grid, rather than hidden site navigation that needs a mobile panel.
Exact flagged Template name is document metadata, not a personal email address. Rendering proves labelled text input with Newsletter value and no email-purpose token.
Exact draft preview intentionally blocks authentication, redirect/notFound and current record resolution before response flush. Adding Suspense here would change intended HTTP/auth behavior.

Core explicitly requires one shared base-maia components.json in packages/ui and rejects app-local copies. The scanner checks only the application-local file and misses that enforced monorepo ownership.

This private application retains its existing noindex publication policy. A public social preview is not a required private-workspace feature, so no public image/card is introduced solely for the scanner score.

PendingApprovalsSection consumes the same query as the mounted ApprovalBudgetSummary sibling. During loading, that sibling renders a status region saying Loading approval and budget policy. The real panel test verifies that announcement while the approval-request skeleton is pending and no false empty queue is shown. The scanner searches only the extracted queue function.
The application deliberately forces the light theme. A global dark-mode shortcut would contradict the mounted provider contract, so it is intentionally omitted.

The extracted note composer calls onSave; its owning saveNote trims the body and returns before mutation for blank input. The submit control is disabled for empty or whitespace-only bodies and while saving. The actual drawer tests exercise whitespace submission through the form and successful persistence to the captured record. The scanner cannot follow the callback boundary.

The donor dashboard layout renders DonorPortalHeader, which mounts the shared NavigationCommandPalette inside its existing action group. It reuses SECTIONS plus Settings and router.push for the six owned dashboard destinations. The shared primitive composes CommandDialog, input, empty state and actionable items with guarded Ctrl/Meta+K. Shadscan 0.17.0 inspects app-owned source scopes and misses this shared-package implementation. The cited caller and shared-primitive Vitest suites verify route filtering and selection, Ctrl/Meta+K, Escape focus return, and non-interception of editable drafts and the account menu. No browser verification is claimed.

The flagged onSubmit is the Samson composer. Its Send trigger is disabled whenever a turn is sending, unconfirmed or awaiting its recorded reply, shows the shared Spinner while the request is in flight, locks the draft, and the turn's receipt is announced in a polite live region; a repeated submit is dropped before any request is made. The scanner looks for a pending-named flag in a disabled expression inside Chat and cannot follow the reason it passes to the same-file Composer. The form handlers it would reach next (scope form, ledger search) only prevent native submission: the scope write is a ControlButton with its own disabled and Spinner state, and search is an idempotent read. Reconsider if Send stops depending on the turn state or the composer changes owner.

No command menu exists to open (see command-menu-present), and the Console registers no window or document key listener at all: a Cmd/Ctrl+K handler would be the only global shortcut on a control surface that otherwise acts only on visible, labeled controls (README, Deliberate omissions). apps/factory-console/tests/shell.test.ts fails if a global key listener, a hotkey library or a command menu appears. Reconsider together with command-menu-present.

The private operator Console is a single page: its nine sections are one always-rendered tab list and every action is a visible, labeled control. A command palette would add a second, hidden route to controls that change what the factory does, so none is mounted (README, Deliberate omissions). apps/factory-console/tests/shell.test.ts fails if a command menu or cmdk appears. Reconsider if the sections outgrow one tab list.

The flagged end-state Select is named by SelectControlLabel, the shared wrapper of Base UI Select.Label, which labels its trigger: the rendered combobox is named End state and described by its hint. Every other Console Select is named the same way or by a Label wired through aria-labelledby. The scanner recognizes only Label/FieldLabel htmlFor, aria attributes or text inside the trigger. Reconsider if a Select loses its control label.

IssueSheet's SheetContent renders IssueBody, whose SheetHeader always contains the SheetTitle Issue #n from the first frame, before the issue is read, so the open sheet is a dialog named by that title. The scanner looks for a title inside the same JSX element and does not follow the child component. The run, analysis report and confirmation dialogs hold their titles directly. Reconsider if the title moves behind a condition.

The flagged useQuery reads the single factory snapshot, not a collection. When no observation exists the Console says so: the connection panel reads Last observation: none yet, a failed first read raises an alert, and every snapshot-backed section renders the shared Unavailable note No ... has been read yet instead of an empty table; while the first read is pending those sections announce loading. Collections keep their own empty messages in the owning views (for example No conversations yet). The scanner requires one of its literal phrases in the same file as the query. Reconsider if a view renders a bare empty collection.

The flagged nav is the ledger pager: two buttons and a range that wrap and stay rendered at every width, not site navigation that needs a mobile panel. The Console's sections are one always-rendered tab list in a horizontally scrolling strip, with no menu trigger, sheet or drawer to hide them behind. The scanner accepts always-visible navigation only when it contains links; paging is state, so the pager uses buttons. Verification limit: the unit test asserts what is rendered and that no width-hiding class is present in jsdom, which has no layout; the Console's own Playwright suite runs every section at a phone viewport but lies outside this ledger's test paths.

The Console is never published or shared: its metadata is noindex and nofollow, every page and API request requires owner authentication and it is reached only through the owner's SSH tunnel on loopback. No crawler or link preview can load the page, so an Open Graph or Twitter image would have no reader and is intentionally absent (README, Deliberate omissions). apps/factory-console/tests/shell.test.ts fails if the noindex policy is dropped or a social image is added without review.

The flagged pending text is the reason shown beside the disabled Send button. The same states are announced by live regions the scanner cannot see from inside Chat: the pending read by the shared LoadingRows (role status, polite), a failed read by ErrorNote (role alert), an in-flight or unconfirmed turn by ReceiptView's polite receipt, and the awaited reply by a status paragraph. Repeating the reason in one more live region would announce every change twice. The issue sheet and analysis report dialog announce their pending reads through the same LoadingRows. Reconsider if one of these states loses its region.

The Console acts only on visible, labeled controls and registers no window or document key listener (README, Deliberate omissions): its controls change what the factory does, so it has no global shortcut of any kind, a dark-mode key included. Unlike the product applications it does not force the light theme; the operator switches theme with the shared ThemeToggle in the header. apps/factory-console/tests/shell.test.ts fails if a global key listener appears. Reconsider if the Console ever gains global shortcuts.

Nothing toast-like is mounted in the root layout; the raw message is the scanner's wording when no toast runtime is installed. That absence is deliberate: a control's outcome is the receipt rendered beside the control that requested it, in a polite live region (see toast-provider-present; README, Deliberate omissions), so the layout mounts only the shared ThemeProvider.

The Console deliberately has no toast channel. A control's outcome is the receipt rendered beside the control that requested it (requested, then observed): a polite live region that stays on screen with its request id and a same-id Retry. A toast leaves on a timer and is detached from the control and request it reports, so no toast runtime is installed (README, Deliberate omissions). apps/factory-console/tests/shell.test.ts fails if one is installed or mounted. Reconsider if the Console gains outcomes that have no owning control.
